newsitem.title: USA: Outright crude prices strong in U.S. Gulf activity.
newsitem.headline: Outright crude prices strong in U.S. Gulf activity.

text.p: U.S. cash crude values firmed for outrights Thursday afternoon, while August grade differentials took on a murky tone ahead of pipeline scheduling on Friday, traders said.

At 1515 EDT (1915 GMT), September NYMEX futures were 12 cents higher at $19.75 a barrel, and with the August/September roll figured at minus 25-30 cents, benchmark WTI hovered around $19.45-55 a barrel.
Grade business wound down for August barrels, which will expire on Friday pipeline scheduling day.
"Most business is done, the only deals are scraping around and are pick-up trades," said a cash broker in Texas.
Deals were seen for Midland/WTI at 28 and 27 cents under August WTI/Cushing, West Texas Sour/Midland at -$1.60 and -$1.53 under WTI and Postings Plus at $1.80 and $1.82.
Later deals saw the Aug/Sep roll sell at -25 cents.
Traders said September LLS remained strong for the near-term, with the WT-LLS spread moving out past a 20 cents premium after weakening to only five cents over in the morning.

"Sweet crude is still valuable in the near-term," a trader said. However, the outlook for sour crude grades looks bearish, with prospects for a flood of Iraqi exports in August weighing on an already well-supplied market, traders said.
